source.section: Form OR-40 line 11 and Pub OR-17 PDF p.83 'Social Security benefits'; Pub OR-17 PDF p.106-107 'Retirement income' (credit code 811) worksheet lines 1-12; Form OR-40 lines 7-19, 20, 24-25, 27-29 (PDF p.3-4); instructions PDF p.16 line 17 and Table 5, PDF p.16-17 line 20 and tax tables, PDF p.32 Chart S and Chart J, PDF p.17-18 line 25 and Exemption credit worksheet; Pub OR-17 PDF p.143 marginal rates

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = private pension (person 0) 8,000.00 + taxable interest 22,110.00 + taxable Social Security 1,555.00 = 31,665.00. Social Security gross 10,000.00, federal taxable part 1,555.00 by the federal worksheet. Federal taxable income = 31,665.00 - 31,500.00 federal standard deduction - 2 x 1,600.00 age 65 additional = -3,035.00, floored at 0.00 = 0.00 (the federal senior deduction is ignored). Form OR-40 (filing status married filing jointly): line 7 federal AGI 31,665.00. Line 8 additions (Schedule OR-ASC line A5): other-state bond interest, code 158, 0.00. Line 9 = 31,665.00 + 0.00 = 31,665.00. Line 10 federal tax liability subtraction: the projection leaves it out (not_modelled), 0.00 here; the return subtracts the smaller of the federal tax and the Table 4 maximum, up to 8,500 (4,250 separate). Line 11 Social Security in federal AGI 1,555.00. Line 12 Oregon refund 0.00. Line 13 Schedule OR-ASC line B7: railroad retirement, code 330, 0.00. Line 14 = 0.00 + 1,555.00 + 0.00 + 0.00 = 1,555.00. Line 15 = 31,665.00 - 1,555.00 = 30,110.00. Line 16 itemized 0.00. Line 17 standard deduction 5,670.00 + 2 age 65 box(es) x 1,000.00 = 7,670.00. Line 18 = 7,670.00. Line 19 = 30,110.00 - 7,670.00 = 22,440.00. Line 20: 8,800.00 x 4.75% = 418 + 13,400.00 x 6.75% = 904.5 + 240.00 x 8.75% = 21; total 1343.5, to the cent 1,343.50 (the tax table's J column, row 22,400 to 22,500, gives 1,345; expected keeps the formula). Lines 21-23 0.00. Line 24 = 1,343.50. Line 25 exemption credit: federal AGI 31,665.00 is not more than 200,000.00; 2 x 256.00 = 512.00. Line 27 retirement income credit (code 811) worksheet: line 1 and line 3 retirement income of the eligible individual(s) 8,000.00; line 2 federal pension subtracted 0.00; line 4 15,000.00; line 5 Social Security and railroad 10,000.00; line 6 = 5,000.00; line 7 household income = 31,665.00 - 1,555.00 + 0.00 = 30,110.00; line 8 30,000.00; line 9 = 110.00; line 10 = 5,000.00 - 110.00 = 4,890.00, not below 0; line 11 smaller of 8,000.00 and 4,890.00 = 4,890.00; line 12 = 4,890.00 x 9% = 440.10. Line 28 credits = 512.00 + 440.10 = 952.10. Line 29 and line 31 state income tax = 1,343.50 - 952.10 = 391.40. Code 351 medical subtraction: no medical expenses in the inputs, not modelled. Line 32 kicker comes after this figure and is not applied (not_modelled). Taxable Social Security is taken out of household income, and both spouses' gross benefits reduce the limit.
accepted_approximations: Tax is figured on the exact income; under 50,000 of taxable income the booklet taxes each table row at its middle and rounds, and the Department rounds at each bracket edge.
